record.paper_title: Some open problems and research directions in the mathematical study of fluid dynamics.
record.original_question: For the incompressible Euler equations obtained from the Navier-Stokes equations by setting the viscosity ν equal to 0, do smooth solutions arising from smooth initial data persist smoothly for all time?

evidence.quote: Do smooth solutions of Euler equations persist for all time?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ (or on the three-dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^3$),
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u + \nabla p = 0, \qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0,$$
where $u:\mathbb{R}^3\times[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}^3$ is the velocity field and $p:\mathbb{R}^3\times[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ is the pressure. Suppose the initial data $u_0$ is smooth (i.e. $C^\infty$), divergence-free, and of finite energy (e.g. $u_0\in C^\infty\cap L^2$, or Schwartz, or smooth on $\mathbb{T}^3$).

Question: Does there exist, for every such initial datum $u_0$, a global-in-time smooth solution $u\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3\times[0,\infty))$ of the above system with $u(\cdot,0)=u_0$? Equivalently, can one rule out the formation of a finite-time singularity from smooth initial data?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of global smooth persistence (no finite-time singularity) for the 3D incompressible Euler equations from general smooth, finite-energy initial data on $\mathbb{R}^3$ or $\mathbb{T}^3$ remains a major open problem. Substantial recent progress has been made in special settings — e.g., proofs of finite-time singularity formation for axisymmetric Euler with smooth data in a domain with boundary (Chen–Hou), and for $C^{1,\alpha}$ data — but the general smooth, boundaryless case is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Singularity formation in 3D Euler equations with smooth initial data and boundary
status_evidence.snippet: The problem of singularity formation of the 3D incompressible Euler equations with smooth initial data has remained open since Euler introduced the equations in 1757.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is described as long-standing and open; recent work proves blow-up in the presence of a boundary.

status_evidence.title: Finite Time Singularities to the 3D Incompressible Euler Equations for Solutions in $C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3\setminus\{0\})\cap C^{1,\alpha}\cap L^2$
status_evidence.snippet: Finite-time singularities established for $C^{1,\alpha}$ data with limited smoothness at a point.
status_evidence.claim: Singularity formation is known for less-than-smooth initial data, but the fully smooth case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Existence and smoothness of the Navier–Stokes equations (Clay)
status_evidence.snippet: Global regularity questions for 3D incompressible flow remain among the foremost open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The companion Euler regularity question is widely considered open.
